newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-finmin says snap poll about state reform.
newsitem.headline: French ex-finmin says snap poll about state reform.

text.p: Former finance minister Alain Madelin said on Tuesday that, beyond cutting spending, France needed to roll back a overweight, overly bureaucratic state and slim down the civil service.
Madelin, a free-marketeer ousted by Prime Minister Alain Juppe after a few months as finance minister in 1995, said the coming election campaign should be about reform of the state.
"We have in France an authoritarian, centralised state, with decisions and recommendations which paralyse French society -- hence reform of the state is the big issue," Madelin told RTL radio.

Some see President Jacques Chirac's decision to call an early election on May 25 and June 1 as heralding a swing to the more fervently free-market, hands-off approach of politicians like Madelin if the centre-right coalition is returned to power.
Cutting state spending was not enough in itself to sort out the problem, Madelin said.

Asked about the civil service, he said: "If you put the question like that I'd say recruit civil servants less rapidly -- one instead of two for example would reduce the number of civil servants by 20,000 a year."
It was not clear whether he meant cutting recruitment in half or cutting in half the level of replacement of retiring civil servants.
